provenance: cold-reviewer finding 2 (M2 close-out): check_state() returned True when there was nothing to check, so a step nobody verified was recorded as postcondition_ok: true — and src/browser/agent.py's own docstring claims every step is postcondition-verified. The planner prompt actively encouraged this by telling the model to emit expected_state: null whenever the resulting state could not be known, which on real sites is the common case. Note this plan produces the RIGHT answer: the sort really does run. It is failed anyway, because an unverified state change is not a verified one — the methodology's INCONCLUSIVE-is-not-PASS stance applied to a step.

triage.note: unverified recorded as verified; fix = postcondition_ok null for 'not checked' + the verifier requires every click to be verified. The planner prompt now requires a postcondition on click.
